highlights.title: Apple is all in on AI — its own and everyone else’s
highlights.summary: Apple's latest earnings show how it's continuing to capitalize on the AI boom without busting its budget on the infrastructure spending consuming its competitors. Overall, Apple posted its best-ever fiscal year for revenue and earnings per share.
body: Apple hasn’t disclosed how much of its revenue growth reflects AI demand or higher prices, but its executives clearly see the technology as a way to drive further sales.
During the earnings call, CFO Kevan Parekh cited a “wide range of ways that AI can contribute to revenue growth over time.”

“On the product side, we feel AI offers a compelling reason for customers to upgrade and switch in order to get the latest capabilities,” he said. “And we also feel there’s opportunities across third-party apps and partnerships as well as first-party opportunities.”

Apple can sell its giant user base the devices they use for AI, even if the AI itself comes from someone else. It can collect fees on subscriptions to AI apps. And it can charge customers who want more access to its own AI features.
points: Apple's latest earnings show how it's continuing to capitalize on the AI boom without busting its budget on the infrastructure spending consuming its competitors.

highlights.title: ‘Our Risk, Their Reward’: Zohran Mamdani on AI and Data Centers
highlights.summary: Ahead of the midterms, WIRED talked to New York City’s mayor about data centers, AI in schools, and the future of the Democratic party.
body: If you think you had a wild year, just imagine how New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani must feel.

In October 2025, weeks before his historic election win, WIRED sat down with Mamdani for an interview at his campaign office. I remember, vividly, the energy that he carried into the room. This was a man, after all, who’d just pulled off a stunning political feat, rising from being an unknown to becoming the mayoral front-runner in a matter of months. In part, that was because of his message, which focused squarely on affordability and the working class. But much of Mamdani’s campaign success can be attributed to how that message was delivered, namely through a mastery of social media that made every other politician in America look like they were still figuring out how to open Instagram.

Mamdani, then just about to turn 34, radiated in our first conversation with what I can best describe as a supernatural electricity. It lit up the room, and in a subsequent photo shoot on a bustling Manhattan street, drew passersby as if by magic. New Yorkers hooted and hollered at the candidate who, seemingly overnight, had made the mundanity of local politics feel like a cultural revolution.
points: Ahead of the midterms, WIRED talked to New York City’s mayor about data centers, AI in schools, and the future of the Democratic party.

That's because William Saliba - a key figure in the Gunners' title win last season - is back in training, having missed the entire campaign so far because of a back injury following his early withdrawal in France's World Cup semi-final loss to Spain.

The 25-year-old has been one of the Premier League's top defenders in recent seasons but - in his absence - summer signing Ezri Konsa has stepped in seamlessly to help Arsenal back to the top of the table.

highlights.title: Should California Subsidize Noah Wyle’s ‘The Pitt’ Pay?
highlights.summary: Gov. Gavin Newsom’s $1 billion proposal to save Hollywood includes so-called "above-the-line” costs (a.k.a. big salaries) as qualified expenditures for a tax credit. That’s been a controversial idea in the state for a long time.
body: For nearly 20 years, California has drawn a line between subsidizing pay for people in front of the camera and the workforce behind it.

When the state started writing checks to Hollywood in 2009, the thinking was that the purpose of tax credits for films and TV shows would be to create jobs and juice the overall economy. That hasn’t changed through four iterations of the program across three governors. Its refusal to offset a production’s salary for, say, Tom Cruise, has made it an outlier among the 39 states that offer production incentives and is probably the biggest reason why it’s losing its grip as the filming capital of the world.

Now — in a major pivot from its historic position that allowing productions to count so-called “above-the-line” spending toward expenditures for filming subsidies would be irresponsible — California is doing the math. Select lawmakers have come to a not-so-surprising conclusion among industry insiders: the state can no longer afford not to.
“We’re still not competitive,” says Assemblymember Rick Chavez Zbur, a key legislator who has been working with Hollywood proponents to fine-tune the state’s incentive program.

highlights.title: How “reverse game theory” could keep AI agents in check
highlights.summary: A new approach known as “reverse game theory” aims to control powerful AI models by designing systems that incentivize them to stick to the rules. As AI models become more capable, safety researchers are scrambling to ensure they are “aligned” with human desires—to make sure, in other words, that…
body: Until now, this work has mostly focused on trying to peer into an AI’s “brain” to understand what it is “thinking,” or training models to hew to values that we hold dear. Claude, for instance, has its constitution —a sort of moral code.
The trouble is, these techniques don’t seem to work particularly well: Models have been shown to deliberately underperform on tests, hide their intentions, and mislead their evaluators.

Now some alignment researchers believe that reverse game theory, also known as mechanism design, might get better results. Where game theory tries to predict how rational actors will behave when given a particular set of rules, reverse game theory attempts to design rules that will elicit the kinds of behavior we want to encourage.

highlights.title: They fell in love on The Simpsons and married in real life. Meet the French Homer and Marge
highlights.summary: They have brought TV’s most famous cartoon couple to life in France for the last 38 years. Philippe Peythieu and Véronique Augereau tell all about working and living together for so long, still being lovebirds – and rarely arguing.
body: The Simpsons is the biggest cartoon comedy in the world, with suburban couple Homer and Marge at its heart. From their beginnings as high-school sweethearts to the travails of married life, they’re an unbreakable pair. Gag-heavy as it may be, it’s also a series with plenty of sentimental plots, from Homer giving up his beloved Duff beer for a month to prove his love to Marge, to Marge composing a heartfelt poem to a dying Homer (miraculously, he makes it through his sushi-induced food poisoning).

Not even the temptations of a brunch-loving bowling instructor called Jacques or a doughnut-guzzling redhead called Mindy could get between them. Plus, of course, they enjoy the occasional “snuggle” (even on a miniature golf course … ).

Now in its 38th season, The Simpsons has also been a huge hit across the globe, meaning hundreds of international actors have voiced this much-loved couple. Among them are Philippe Peythieu and Véronique Augereau, who – as well as playing Marge and Homer in the French dub of The Simpsons since 1990 – met through the show and ended up getting married.

highlights.summary: Bethesda is officially confirming today that the next Elder Scrolls game will be called The Elder Scrolls VI Sentinel. The confirmation came in a less than 10-minute video celebrating 40 years of Bethesda game studios.
body: It’s been more than eight years since Bethesda officially announced the existence of the sixth game in its Elder Scrolls series, and studio chief Todd Howard made the announcement today and called it the “perfect time” to fully name the game.
Bethesda isn’t sharing any more details on The Elder Scrolls VI Sentinel today, though. The Xbox Wire press release on the name is literally just a picture of the logo.

I reported in Notepad last week that Bethesda was planning to name the game in November, during a period that will mark 15 years since The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim was released. Sentinel will be set in Hammerfell, a province in the Elder Scrolls universe that’s appeared in The Elder Scrolls Adventures: Redguard and The Elder Scrolls Online. Sentinel will be the first game about the history of the Elder Scrolls, and help uncover the secrets of these mysterious ancient artifacts.

highlights.title: Scrum, foul play, TMO - what can we expect from refs this autumn?
highlights.summary: World Rugby has laid out a vision of a safer and more continuous sport, but with a desire to "embrace the contest" around the breakdown and set-piece.
body: The number of tries in international rugby has rocketed from six to eight per match in the space of just two years as World Rugby looks to futureproof the game.

As part of the manifesto, the sport's world governing body will ramp up fan engagement and has launched a study using biometric sensors to find out what excites and invigorates supporters during matches.
Before the return of the Nations Championship, the top 24 international head coaches met with World Rugby officials outside London to discuss how the game will look over the coming month.
According to World Rugby sources, the coaches highlighted a number of "grey areas"; for example the scrum and breakdown, deliberate knock-ons and foul play in the act of scoring.

highlights.title: Scream Star Confirms She’s Returning for Sequel
highlights.summary: One of the definitive scream queens is coming back for another night with Ghostface. Neve Campbell confirmed she will return as Sidney Prescott (now Evans) in Scream 8.
body: “ Scream 8, that’s in the pipeline as well,” Campbell said to AP. “You know I can’t tell you anything about Scream 8, ” the actress said, “I’ll be in it.” Campbell has appeared in every film in the series except 2023’s Scream 6.

Paramount and Spyglass announced that they would begin developing an eighth movie on March 31, 2026, with sisters Lilla and Nora Zuckerman handling the script. The Zuckermans are television writers who have worked together on series like Poker Face, Suits, Fringe, Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., and more.

It isn’t particularly surprising that another Scream film is on the way. Earlier this year, Scream 7 became the highest-grossing movie in the series’ history, bringing in $214 million against a $45 million budget. Series creator Kevin Williamson directed and co-wrote the picture.

However, despite its big-box office performance, critics almost universally panned the film, calling it shallow and the franchise's worst entry. It has a 29% score on Rotten Tomatoes, putting it dead last on the Tomatometer behind Scream 3, the only other series installment with a negative score on the review aggregator.

highlights.title: I spent 11 years without my childhood friend. Finding our way back together was staggeringly simple
highlights.summary: I thought about her a lot after our friendship imploded. When our birthdays rolled around, I wondered what we’d be doing if we were still in touch. I was 26 when I lost my childhood friend. By that point, I’d known her for almost two-thirds of my life.
body: Our first conversation was at an ice-skating party when we were nine years old. I’d been nervous in the weeks leading up to the party because I couldn’t ice-skate. Every time the Spice Girls’ 2 Become 1 music video came on, the sight of Victoria Beckham singing on an ice rink filled me with impending doom. I was sure I would disgrace myself at the party.

But the party – and I don’t often say this about parties – was a blast. As it turned out, my in-line skating experience gave me some advantage on the ice, and I met a girl who was easy to talk to. I was a shy child, so I was struck by that sense of ease – how I wasn’t panicking about what to say or lurking awkwardly on the edge of a conversation. I can’t remember what we talked about. She was kind enough not to mention the fact I’d chosen to wear a dolphin-print sarong. We held hands and at one point she asked: “What’s your name again?” Apparently, we’d had so much to say to each other, we’d skated right over all the usual greetings and pleasantries.

When our birthdays rolled around, I wondered what we’d be doing if we were still in touch.

highlights.title: OpenAI is quietly renaming data centers ‘compute campuses’
highlights.summary: People hate data centers. They're loud, resource-hungry eyesores that are so profoundly unpopular they have managed to achieve the near-impossible in today's polarized political landscape: genuine bipartisan opposition. But what about "compute campuses"? Those sound lovely, right?
body: Critics say OpenAI should tackle peoples’ concerns about data centers, not rebrand them.
OpenAI seems to be gambling that a quiet rebrand could be all it takes to defuse the growing political backlash that threatens to derail the infrastructure fueling the AI boom.

OpenAI debuted the new terminology on Monday in an announcement launching its new “Grid Protectors Program.” The initiative, starting with an upcoming site in Effingham County, Georgia, aims to address concerns about the strain its sprawling AI infrastructure places on local power grids, particularly during extreme weather and emergencies. It’s a familiar data center problem. Yet in the roughly 900 word announcement, the term “data center” appeared just twice, outnumbered by “compute campus.”

highlights.title: One Popular PC Game Storefront Has Had Enough Of AI Slop, And It’s Taking Action
highlights.summary: Indie game storefront Itch.io has announced it removed "a couple terabytes of AI slop" and has begun taking steps to combat the deluge of AI-created games appearing on the platform.
body: The platform had already noted that the number of game pages being created per day had doubled from 3,000 to 6,000 over the last two months, with reports of users flooding the game uploads page with dozens of AI-created game spams. Going forward, Itch says that these sorts of bulk uploads will result in that spam being de-indexed, and filtering for generative AI disclosure will be added more sections of the site, including the search results page.

This doesn't mean Itch is outright banning AI-generated content, but it is taking a harder line against people who spam the site with it. In its official terms and conditions, Itch states that if the use of AI in a game is "clearly stated" and if "it adds substantial value" to the user experience, then that's okay. But if you're uploading something iterative, that'll be against the platform's rules.

highlights.summary: Slowly cooked, sticky sausages sauteed with onion, soy and perhaps a bit of Marmite … our panel even has bangers with bangs for bonfire night. What are the best, comforting sausage dinners for autumn?
body: Another one-pan job is pigs and figs. “That’s a really lovely combination,” says Ben Tish, chef/director of the Cubitt House group of pubs in London. “Roast some sausages, then add figs and cook until they’re nice and jammy.” Go in with a bit of red wine and red-wine vinegar to deglaze the pan, “then chuck in a handful of cooked borlotti beans, a little stock and some herbs, and leave to simmer and come together”.

We’re also entering ragu time of year, so it’s also worth considering swapping mince for sausages. “Open them up, scoop out the meat and roast in a hot oven until the sausagemeat clumps up,” says Nye Smith, head chef of The Three Horseshoes in Somerset. “Braise that in a tomatoey, red wine base, or cook with white wine, fennel, dark greens [think cavolo nero] and a splash of cream.” After that, just add cooked pasta or gnocchi.

highlights.title: EPA throws in the towel on policing air pollution from factory farms
highlights.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency late last week announced it would end a 20-plus-year effort to develop methods to monitor air pollution from factory farms, effectively shuttering the agency’s stop-and-start attempts to regulate the potentially pollutant-spewing facilities under the Clean Air…
body: The announcement came just days before the midterm elections and was characterized by the agency as a long-awaited reprieve for farmers, a historically important constituency for Trump and the Republican Party.

When tens of thousands of animals are packed into one place, pollution from their waste is blown from ventilation fans or emanates from giant lagoons of liquid effluent. Livestock facilities emit fine particulate matter, ammonia, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide, and volatile organic compounds, all contributing to a toxic mix. Research has shown that emissions from these operations are a major cause of air pollution, causing nearly 12,700 deaths in the United States a year.

Strictly speaking, concentrated animal feeding operations, or CAFOs, are required to get permits under the Clean Air Act and report emissions of these pollutants under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability and Act and the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act. But through a deal crafted in tandem with the EPA and the livestock industry, they’ve been given amnesty from doing so for more than 20 years.
